programs.program: Sound Design for Audiovisual Media (Sound / Ton)
programs.university: Filmuniversität Babelsberg KONRAD WOLF
programs.institutionType: Public film school (film university)
programs.durationEcts: Programme page states 6 semesters / 120 LP (ECTS). The 6-semester figure is unusual for a 120-LP master — confirm with the programme office.
programs.language: German (DSH-1 German certificate is a hard admission condition)
programs.focus: Film/Game Sound; Sound Design; Recording/Engineering; Immersive Audio
programs.whatYouStudy: Four core domains: audio engineering, sound mixing, acoustics/signal processing, and music. Students plan and deliver cinema sound mixes and act as sound supervisors on real film productions, building an individual 'sound language' through interdisciplinary artistic projects. Heavy Pro Tools use (the entrance exam itself is a Pro Tools scoring task). Strong industry pipeline into Babelsberg Studios.
programs.entryRequirements: Completed B.F.A. in Sound, a Tonmeister degree, or a comparable subject-specific degree; uni-assist evaluation for foreign qualifications; German at DSH-1 minimum; medical certificate of normal hearing plus an audiogram, both issued within the last year.
programs.acceptsNonMusic: No. The page requires a "completed Bachelor of Fine Arts in Sound, Tonmeister, or comparable subject-specific degree". A software-engineering BSc is not a comparable subject-specific degree, and no alternative talent route is offered.
programs.portfolioSpec: Documentation of works from the past three years, max 12 pages (PDF). Video compilation of at least THREE films on which the applicant did the sound design, 15 minutes total (MPG/MPEG/MP4/MOV/WMV, max 3.5 GB). At least ONE piece of music recorded or mixed by the applicant (WAV/MP3/MP4, max 5 GB). Tabular CV describing musical development.
programs.auditionSpec: On-site three-part aptitude test: (1) music test — intervals, harmonies, piano audition, critical listening/audio evaluation; (2) interview — presentation of submitted work plus subject knowledge; (3) practical exam — scoring a scene in Pro Tools.
programs.applicationOpens: 12 April (per the programme's own application page)
programs.deadline: 18 May 2027 for the winter-semester 2027/28 intake, as published on the application page. Verify directly — the page may still be showing an earlier cycle.
programs.tuitionIntl: No tuition (Brandenburg public institution). Only a semester contribution/administrative fee; exact amount UNVERIFIED.
programs.scholarship: DAAD Study Scholarships – Master Studies (open to Tunisian graduates; funding usually starts 1 October); Deutschlandstipendium
programs.stipend: DAAD graduate scholarship pays a monthly stipend plus travel allowance and health insurance; exact 2027 monthly rate UNVERIFIED. The university itself pays nothing.
programs.facilities: Germany's oldest film school (founded 1954) on the historic Babelsberg Studios site, 30 min from Berlin. Cinema mixing stages, Dolby-standard theatrical mixing, full film-sound post chain. Reported acceptance rate 3–5% (secondary source, UNVERIFIED).
programs.fitNotes: Best-in-class for film sound in Europe, but effectively closed to him: it demands a prior sound/Tonmeister degree, DSH-1 German, an audiogram, and a portfolio of three finished films he has already mixed. Also the wrong target anyway — it trains film sound supervisors, not DJs/producers.

programs.program: Musikregie (Tonmeister) – Master of Music
programs.university: Hochschule für Musik Detmold – Erich-Thienhaus-Institut (ETI)
programs.institutionType: Public conservatory / Musikhochschule
programs.durationEcts: UNVERIFIED (one aggregator lists 1 year; the ETI pages do not state duration or ECTS)
programs.language: German (proof of German required)
programs.focus: Recording/Engineering; Music Production (classical/acoustic recording direction)
programs.whatYouStudy: Artistic recording direction (Musikregie): responsibility for the artistic result and quality of a music production. Combines musical-communicative competence with technical foundations and extensive hands-on practice in the ETI recording studios; work in broadcasting, film and TV, opera houses and theatres. Sister programme Musikübertragung (B.Mus.) is the bachelor-level Tonmeister track; a Music Acoustics M.Sc./Dr.-Ing. also sits at the ETI.
programs.entryRequirements: Bachelor's degree in Music Recording (Musikübertragung) or a Tonmeister diploma; proof of German; proof of health insurance; successful aptitude test.
programs.acceptsNonMusic: No. The requirement is explicitly a "Bachelor's degree in Music Recording respectively diploma in Tonmeister". A music-specific/Tonmeister degree is required; no talent-based exception is published.
programs.portfolioSpec: Tabular CV; written statement explaining the choice of programme and intended study focus; a CD/DVD containing THREE productions made by the applicant within the past year.
programs.auditionSpec: Aptitude test: presentation of the three submitted productions plus a colloquium of approx. 30 minutes covering musical repertoire, technical principles and studio experience. Assessed by at least two committee members as 'qualified' / 'not qualified'.
programs.applicationOpens: 1 October (summer semester) / 15 February (winter semester)
programs.deadline: PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new date: winter semester 15 February–15 March; summer semester 1 October–1 November (as published, no year stated).
programs.tuitionIntl: No tuition (NRW public). Semester fee only; exact amount UNVERIFIED.
programs.scholarship: DAAD Study Scholarships – Master Studies for Artists/All Disciplines; Deutschlandstipendium
programs.facilities: The Erich-Thienhaus-Institut is the internationally leading German Tonmeister school; multiple recording studios and control rooms, strong links to broadcasters, opera houses and labels. Detailed console/immersive-room specs are in a scanned brochure that could not be reliably read — UNVERIFIED.
programs.fitNotes: The gold standard for classical recording engineering in Germany, and completely out of reach for him: it requires a Tonmeister bachelor plus three of his own studio productions from the last 12 months, in German. Also classical-recording-oriented, not electronic/club music. List it as a long-term aspiration, not a 2027 application.

programs.program: Popular Music M.A. – specialisation Producing / Composing Artist
programs.university: Popakademie Baden-Württemberg
programs.institutionType: Public university of popular music (state Hochschule)
programs.durationEcts: 4 semesters / 120 ECTS, full-time
programs.language: German (B2 required of international applicants by the end of the first semester)
programs.focus: Music Production; Electronic Music Production
programs.whatYouStudy: Two-stage structure: year 1 taught courses, year 2 an independent master project. The Producing/Composing track covers songwriting, arrangement, recording, sound design, beat programming, mixing, mastering, electronic music production, film music, game music, vocal producing and music-business practice — plus working as a production service provider for band projects. Facilities include professional recording studios (Tonstudio), the SMIX.LAB and a media library. Germany's only state Hochschule dedicated to popular music.
programs.entryRequirements: Completed first degree with a standard duration of at least 6 semesters; advanced practical musical experience; department-specific entrance examination; German B2 for international applicants by the end of the first semester.
programs.acceptsNonMusic: Check. The published requirement is only "a completed undergraduate degree with a minimum standard study duration of 6 semesters" — no subject restriction is stated, so his BSc Software Engineering satisfies the formal condition. Admission is decided almost entirely by the practical entrance exam, which does demand advanced musical ability.
programs.portfolioSpec: Upload of own musical productions; for performing/educating artists at least one live video (max 200 MB). Additional accepted material: videos, press coverage, photographs, cover artwork, scores, lyrics, teaching concepts. Exact number of tracks required for Producing/Composing is not specified on the application page — UNVERIFIED.
programs.auditionSpec: Live entrance examination (Aufnahmeprüfung), format varies by department. Typically 2–3 pieces performed, often the applicant's own compositions, with up to three accompanying musicians or playback; plus theory examination, improvisation test and interview.
programs.applicationOpens: UNVERIFIED (portal typically opens in the winter preceding the deadline)
programs.deadline: PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new date: 30 April (23:59 UTC upload deadline) for the following winter semester.
programs.tuitionIntl: No tuition for a first degree at the Popakademie itself, BUT Baden-Württemberg's LHGebG charges non-EU/EEA international students €1,500 per semester (≈€6,000 over 4 semesters). As a Tunisian national he falls under this fee.
programs.scholarship: DAAD Study Scholarships – Master Studies (Tunisia eligible); Deutschlandstipendium. No Popakademie-specific scholarship found.
programs.facilities: Professional recording studios, SMIX.LAB, mediathek; faculty of working industry producers; located in Mannheim's Musikpark start-up cluster with dense German music-industry links.
programs.fitNotes: The single closest match in Germany to "I want to be a producer": actual beat programming, electronic production, mixing and mastering, taught by industry practitioners. Two obstacles: German B2 and a genuinely demanding live entrance exam, plus €1,500/semester as a non-EU student. He should treat this as his main German target and spend 2026–27 building a producer audition set and German.

programs.program: Filmton / Sounddesign (Diplomaufbaustudium – postgraduate diploma at master level)
programs.university: Filmakademie Baden-Württemberg
programs.institutionType: Public film school (state-owned GmbH)
programs.durationEcts: 4 semesters plus 1 diploma semester (5 semesters total); ECTS not published — UNVERIFIED
programs.language: German; English in project studies (PS)
programs.focus: Film/Game Sound; Sound Design; Immersive Audio
programs.whatYouStudy: Year 1 concentrates on production/location sound; year 2 on post-production. Covers original sound recording on set, sound design, dialogue editing, mixing technique, working with Foley artists, film-music recording and Dolby Atmos. Optional specialisations in media design and sound for games. Entirely project-based — students score the academy's own film productions.
programs.entryRequirements: Postgraduate (Aufbaustudium) structure implies a completed prior degree; Hochschulreife plus, where held, officially certified Vordiplom/Diplom/Bachelor/Master must be submitted. No music degree is demanded.
programs.acceptsNonMusic: Check — most likely yes. It is a Diplomaufbaustudium with no stated subject restriction and no explicit prohibition on non-music backgrounds; the filter is the practical entrance exam, not the bachelor subject. Confirm in writing before applying.
programs.portfolioSpec: Own projects/work samples uploaded via the online portal. Video work samples: max 1 GB, MP4 container, H.264 codec, data rate 15 MB/s. Exact number and duration of required audio samples not published — UNVERIFIED.
programs.auditionSpec: Pre-selection on the file, then an on-site entrance examination (Aufnahmeprüfung) conducted in Pro Tools. Applicants must bring working knowledge of recording, sound design, mixing and bouncing.
programs.applicationOpens: UNVERIFIED (online portal typically opens in the autumn)
programs.deadline: PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new date: 15 February.
programs.tuitionIntl: €0 for EU citizens; €1,500 for non-EU citizens per the programme page (whether this is per semester under the BW LHGebG or a one-off is not clarified on the page — confirm).
programs.scholarship: DAAD Study Scholarships (Film/Fine Art strand); Deutschlandstipendium. No academy-specific scholarship found.
programs.facilities: State-of-the-art audio post-production studios and current-industry on-set equipment, Dolby Atmos mixing, Foley stage; part of one of Europe's most production-active film schools with heavy German TV/film industry placement.
programs.fitNotes: The most realistic German film-sound route for someone without a music degree — the gate is a Pro Tools practical test rather than a conservatory audition, and the fee is low. But it makes film/game sound designers, not DJs. Worth applying only if he genuinely wants a screen-audio career alongside producing.

programs.program: Zeitabhängige Medien / Sound – Vision (sub-programme of Sound–Vision–Games)
programs.university: HAW Hamburg – Hochschule für Angewandte Wissenschaften, Dept. Medientechnik
programs.institutionType: University of applied sciences (public)
programs.durationEcts: 3 semesters (90 ECTS per aggregator; the HAW page states 3 semesters, ECTS UNVERIFIED on the official page)
programs.language: German (C1 required); English B1 also tested at interview
programs.focus: Sound Design; Immersive Audio; Recording/Engineering; Live/Event audio
programs.whatYouStudy: Project-centred study at the intersection of science, technology and creative design. Modules cover audio technology and sound design, video technology and image design, VFX production, interactive design, lighting technology and design, plus production and project management. Eight required/elective modules in the chosen branch. Graduates go into audio/video/lighting manufacturers, production studios and theatres. Nationally unique in linking sound, moving image and games.
programs.entryRequirements: Bachelor's degree with at least 210 ECTS in media technology, media systems, computer science, IT (applied IT or media specialism welcome), communication design, illustration or a related subject; German C1; English B1; passed aptitude test.
programs.acceptsNonMusic: Yes — explicitly. The accepted-degree list names "computer science, IT (applicants with a degree in applied IT or with a specialism in media are welcome)". Caveat: it requires 210 ECTS, and many 3-year BSc degrees are 180 ECTS — he must check his SMU MedTech credit total.
programs.portfolioSpec: Between 3 and 10 work samples that "demonstrate your interest in and your aptitude and potential for your chosen branch" in detail and comprehensively. Accepted types: video, animation, light design, light installation, sound design, soundscape, music production, installation, performance, interactive/multimedia work.
programs.auditionSpec: Two-stage aptitude assessment: (1) portfolio/work-sample review; (2) interview if stage 1 is passed, at which German C1 and English B1 are verified. No instrumental audition.
programs.applicationOpens: 1 October (registration for the aptitude test)
programs.deadline: PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new date: aptitude-test registration 1–31 October (one source says 'until 14 October'); formal application for the study place 1 December–15 January; entry SUMMER semester only, starting early April.
programs.tuitionIntl: No tuition. Semester contribution €397, including the semester ticket and the Germany-wide rail pass (Deutschlandticket).
programs.scholarship: DAAD Study Scholarships – Master Studies for All Academic Disciplines; Deutschlandstipendium
programs.facilities: Art and Media Campus Finkenau, Hamburg: audio, video and lighting labs, studios for sound design and interactive media. Facility detail beyond the campus address is UNVERIFIED.
programs.fitNotes: Structurally the friendliest German public option for a software-engineering graduate — CS degrees are named as welcome, the gate is a portfolio not an audition, and the total cost is €397 a semester. Two catches: German C1 (high), and the intake is April only, so a September 2027 start is impossible — he would target April 2027 (apply Oct 2026–Jan 2027) or April 2028. It is also more media/event technology than club-music production.

programs.program: Integrative Komposition (M.Mus.) – specialisation Elektronische Komposition (ICEM)
programs.university: Folkwang Universität der Künste
programs.institutionType: Public art university (music, theatre, dance, design)
programs.durationEcts: 4 semesters full-time (part-time possible) / 120 ECTS
programs.language: German (B1 required at enrolment)
programs.focus: Electronic Music / Live Electronics; Electroacoustic Composition; Sonic Arts
programs.whatYouStudy: Project-oriented master built around the student's own artistic development project. Four combinable specialisations: Electronic Composition, Instrumental Composition, Pop Composition, and Composition & Visualisation — students may mix them with different weightings. Teaching happens in the ICEM (Institut für Computermusik und Elektronische Medien), which has trained electroacoustic composers since 1971 and shaped the current Integrative Komposition degrees.
programs.entryRequirements: A first university degree on which the master builds, OR proof of outstanding artistic talent; artistic aptitude established through the Eignungsprüfung; German B1 at enrolment; €50 application fee.
programs.acceptsNonMusic: Yes, in practice. The page states applicants need "a first university degree which the Master study course is based on" and separately allows entry on "proof of outstanding artistic talent"; the programme welcomes non-music backgrounds provided artistic aptitude is proven. The portfolio, not the degree subject, decides.
programs.portfolioSpec: Stage-1 digital submission of own works "in the form of original scores (especially for instrumental composition), recordings, videos etc." PLUS a concept/project plan for an artistic development project describing the intended master-thesis topic. Formats PDF and MP4, max 100 MB total. No fixed number of works is stated.
programs.auditionSpec: Two-stage Eignungsprüfung. Stage 1: digital preliminary round — portfolio and master-project draft assessed for technical/artistic ability and feasibility. Stage 2: in-person main round — approx. 30-minute colloquium on the submitted works, any revisions, artistic development and engagement with current artistic trends.
programs.applicationOpens: UNVERIFIED
programs.deadline: PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new date: 15 March for the following winter semester; 15 November for the following summer semester.
programs.tuitionIntl: No tuition (NRW). €50 application fee plus the semester social contribution (Studierendenwerk + NRW semester ticket); amount UNVERIFIED.
programs.scholarship: DAAD Study Scholarships – Master Studies for Artists (Music strand), Tunisia eligible; Deutschlandstipendium
programs.facilities: ICEM — one of Germany's oldest and most respected computer-music/electronic-media institutes (studio for live-electronic music since 1971), with a historic technical instrument collection; regular PACT Zollverein collaborations.
programs.fitNotes: A genuinely open door: no music degree strictly required, the decision rests on a portfolio plus a project concept, and it is tuition-free. But this is art-music electronic composition (electroacoustic, live electronics, installation), not dance-floor production — he would need to frame his work as compositional practice, and reach German B1.

programs.program: Elektronische Komposition – Master of Music
programs.university: Hochschule für Musik und Tanz Köln (HfMT Köln)
programs.institutionType: Public conservatory (Europe's largest music academy)
programs.durationEcts: 4 semesters / 120 ECTS
programs.language: German (minimum A2 for non-German speakers)
programs.focus: Electronic Music / Live Electronics; Electroacoustic Composition
programs.whatYouStudy: Independent compositional work and professionalisation: mixed instrumental/electronic composition, installations and internet works, plus self-organised concerts of student-created music. The electronic and instrumental composition classes work closely together, so students can join the other class's projects and take main-subject lessons there. All practical work takes place in the Studio für Elektronische Musik.

programs.acceptsNonMusic: Essentially No. The page states that "Bachelor graduates from other art or computer science fields" are admitted only "in exceptional cases of exceptional talent". Computer science is named — but as an exception route requiring exceptional demonstrated talent, not a normal pathway.
programs.portfolioSpec: Own works must be submitted for evaluation and are presented and discussed at the colloquium. The specific number, duration and format of works is not stated on the programme page — UNVERIFIED (submission runs through the muvac platform).
programs.auditionSpec: Qualifying examination consisting of a colloquium: presentation and discussion of the submitted works, with questions on the applicant's own musical aesthetics and prior knowledge of contemporary music. No instrumental audition mentioned.
programs.applicationOpens: UNVERIFIED
programs.deadline: UNVERIFIED — no deadline published on the programme page; applications run through muvac. Confirm with the Studio für Elektronische Musik.
programs.tuitionIntl: No tuition (NRW). Semester social contribution only; amount UNVERIFIED.
programs.scholarship: DAAD Study Scholarships – Master Studies for Artists (Music); Deutschlandstipendium
programs.facilities: Studio für Elektronische Musik with several fixed and mobile workstations, comprehensive software/hardware and "excellent listening facilities"; Cologne is the historic home of the legendary WDR Studio for Electronic Music (Stockhausen).
programs.fitNotes: Prestigious and free, and the German bar is unusually low (A2). But the entry wording is the problem: without a composition bachelor he lands in the "exceptional talent" exception, which is a very high evidentiary bar for someone with no prior music training. Also purely art-music, no production/DJ content.

programs.program: Multimedia Composition (Multimediale Komposition) – Master
programs.university: Hochschule für Musik und Theater Hamburg (HfMT Hamburg)
programs.institutionType: Public conservatory / Musikhochschule
programs.durationEcts: 2 years (4 semesters) / 120 ECTS
programs.language: English (the entrance examination is conducted in English). German B2 reported as required of international applicants by a secondary source — confirm with the Hochschule.
programs.focus: Electronic Music / Live Electronics; Sonic Arts; Immersive/Interactive Audio
programs.whatYouStudy: Interdisciplinary programme for composers, media artists and computer scientists with musical interests. Fields: algorithmic composition, live electronics, game-engine development, video and light programming, digital recording, interactive installations, microtonal composition. Software explicitly taught: Max/MSP/Jitter, Ableton Live, Unreal Engine, MadMapper, TouchDesigner, Lightkey. Access to an AV Media Center and a digital recording studio.

The programme is described as "aimed at applicants with a completed Bachelor's degree in music, composition, media art, or computer science" and is "designed for composers, media artists, and computer scientists with musical interests". A software-engineering BSc is squarely within scope.
programs.portfolioSpec: "At least three representative works which demonstrate the ability to artistically incorporate the use of digital media, especially in the field of computer music. These works can be in the form of scores, texts, recordings, computer programs, videos, etc. and/or interactive websites."
programs.auditionSpec: Two-part entrance examination: (1) a 3-hour written exam — interactive computer-music tasks, text analysis, and multiple-choice questions on digital-media terminology; (2) a 15-minute interview about the submitted work and the applicant's motivation. No instrumental audition.
programs.applicationOpens: UNVERIFIED
programs.deadline: UNVERIFIED — the programme page gives no deadline; applications are made online via the HfMT portal for the winter semester. Contact the department office.
programs.tuitionIntl: No tuition (Hamburg public). Semester contribution only; amount UNVERIFIED.
programs.scholarship: DAAD Study Scholarships – Master Studies (Music / All Disciplines), Tunisia eligible; Deutschlandstipendium
programs.facilities: AV Media Center and digital recording studio; Hamburg's Musikhochschule sits in a city with a very strong electronic/club scene. Studio detail beyond this is UNVERIFIED.
programs.fitNotes: The strongest realistic German target for him alongside the Popakademie: a CS bachelor is explicitly welcome, the portfolio can include code and interactive work as well as tracks, the entrance test rewards technical ability over conservatory ear-training, and instruction is in English. Caveat: it is computer music / installation / live electronics, not commercial dance production — he must be genuinely interested in Max/MSP and algorithmic work, and should confirm the German requirement.

programs.program: Künstlerische Musikproduktion (Artistic Music Production) – Master of Music
programs.university: Robert Schumann Hochschule Düsseldorf – Institut für Musik und Medien (IMM)
programs.institutionType: Public conservatory / Musikhochschule

programs.auditionSpec: "The proficiency test involves the evaluation of work samples to be submitted in advance as well as completion of an instrumental/vocal audition. In addition, there is a practical task in the intended major as well as written examinations of musical and technical hearing ability." Test fee €50.
programs.applicationOpens: UNVERIFIED

programs.program: Klang und Realität (Sound and Reality) – Master of Music
programs.university: Robert Schumann Hochschule Düsseldorf – Institut für Musik und Medien (IMM)
programs.institutionType: Public conservatory / Musikhochschule
programs.durationEcts: 4 semesters / 120 ECTS, full-time
programs.language: German (B2, Goethe-Institut standard)
programs.focus: Sonic Arts (practice-based); Electronic Music / Live Electronics
programs.whatYouStudy: Project-driven master integrating performative, compositional and algorithmic forms of contemporary art. Own projects sit at the centre and are re-conceptualised across two years on the basis of critical, multi-perspectival peer feedback. Two focus areas: Epistemic Media (art as a method of enquiry — acoustic research, documentary film, algorithmic composition) and Transmedia Forms (performance, sound art, installation, digital media). Accordingly, the master's program is open to students from all disciplinary backgrounds." This is the clearest published welcome to a non-music graduate of any German programme found.
programs.portfolioSpec: A detailed project proposal demonstrating the applicant's interests, motivations and skills, submitted with the portfolio. Number/length of accompanying works not specified — UNVERIFIED.
programs.auditionSpec: Portfolio- and proposal-based aptitude assessment (Eignungsprüfung). No traditional instrumental entrance exam is mentioned.
programs.applicationOpens: UNVERIFIED
programs.deadline: PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new date: 31 October, once a year. SUMMER semester entry only — courses begin at the start of April.
programs.tuitionIntl: No tuition (NRW). Semester contribution plus €50 proficiency-test fee; contribution amount UNVERIFIED.
programs.scholarship: DAAD Study Scholarships – Master Studies; Deutschlandstipendium
programs.facilities: Institut für Musik und Medien studios and collaborative project spaces; detail UNVERIFIED.
programs.fitNotes: Formally the easiest German conservatory master for him to enter — open to all disciplinary backgrounds, assessed on a project proposal, no audition, no tuition. But it is artistic-research and transmedia work, not production craft: he would leave with a conceptual sound-art practice, not DJ/producer chops. Ableton Certified Training centre. Berlin's electronic-music ecosystem is on the doorstep.

Two serious caveats: it costs roughly €12,600 for the full-time year with no funding available to him, and the school explicitly says it is artistic research, not vocational production training. Label this the self-pay fallback; the Berlin network may nonetheless be worth more to a DJ career than any degree on this list.

programs.whatYouStudy: Four intertwined strands: computer music composition; performance and interpretation of electronic works; conception and development of new electronic instruments; and music informatics. Plus history, theory and aesthetics of computer music, and (master level) methods of artistic-scientific research. IEM is one of Europe's leading centres for Ambisonics/spatial audio research and runs its own well-known open-source plug-in suite and multichannel performance spaces; graduates are prepared for music, art, media and the creative industries.

programs.portfolioSpec: Two meaningful examples of your own artistic work ("zwei aussagekräftige Beispiele deiner künstlerischen Arbeit"), approx. 5 minutes each, as audio or video documents. Multichannel material must be reduced to stereo. Total upload not more than approx. 150 MB, uploaded before the registration deadline. Works may be compositions with electroacoustic means, sound installations, documentation of performances/interpretations of computer-music works, development of computer-music instruments, or music-informatics applications.
programs.auditionSpec: No live/on-site audition. The exam is a colloquium/interview held via Zoom in German or English, discussing the submitted works, your motivation, interests and intended area of specialisation. No instrument required.

programs.institutionType: Public university of music and performing arts

programs.whatYouStudy: Managing complex audio productions end to end — artistic-technical planning, creative realisation, completion — with a large elective share so you sharpen an individual artistic profile within one of three specialisations: classical music production, popular-music production, or film sound. Sound reinforcement and sound design can be taken as additional emphases regardless of specialisation. A master project is central.
programs.entryRequirements: Passed admission examination; a completed subject-relevant bachelor's or diploma degree; proof of German at B2; and proof of unimpaired hearing. The admission info sheet is explicit: you must upload "Nachweis über ein abgeschlossenes Studium (Bachelor o. Diplom) in einem facheinschlägigen Studium Tonmeister_in" — i.e. a Tonmeister-type degree. Also required: a current specialist medical certificate with audiogram (not older than two months) confirming physiologically unimpaired hearing across 125–8,000 Hz.
programs.portfolioSpec: Very heavy and fully specified. (a) Motivation video, max 3 minutes, answering a fixed question list for your specialisation. (b) Instrument/voice video: for Popularmusik, 2 jazz/popular works with improvisation or ad libs (an own composition is allowed; for piano, one piece may be improvisation using keyboards/synths/DAWs such as Ableton Live with clearly audible playing craft and own sound design); band or play-alongs permitted; total video duration max 15 minutes. (c) Piano video if piano is not your main instrument. (d) PORTFOLIO — Popularmusik: SIX popular-music productions in different styles, produced, recorded and mixed substantially by you, at least three with vocals and at least two involving recording of acoustic instruments, all delivered as stereo audio (5.1/Dolby Atmos versions optional), each at least 2:30 and max 30 minutes in total, plus written documentation of 7,000–12,000 characters (approach, microphone choices, session photos, DAW screenshots, challenges, critical reflection). Klassik: three music-recording projects, two pure stereo audio productions with different ensembles plus one free project (audio or video, stereo/5.1/Dolby Atmos, with a stereo version supplied), total 20–40 minutes, plus the same 7,000–12,000-character documentation. Filmton: three film-sound projects (production sound, sound design, mixing), two with more complex sound design or mixing and one at least in 5.1, plus documentation. Formats: one work per file, .wav (5.1 as labelled single wavs), ADM BWF for Atmos, .mp4/.mov video, max Full HD, max 8 GB per file, documentation as PDF.
programs.auditionSpec: Two-part commission exam. Part 1 is the submitted video/audio package. If the commission invites you, Part 2 is an ON-SITE oral exam at the mdw in Vienna: a practical studio task (e.g. editing, mixing or sound design), questions on music theory and music literature, ear-training tasks, analysis of a listening or film example, questions on acoustics and audio/studio technology, and a technical discussion of your portfolio.

Diplom) in einem facheinschlägigen Studium Tonmeister_in", and the MA page requires "ein facheinschlägiges Bachelorstudium" with the mdw BA Tonmeister_in named as the intended route. A software-engineering BSc does not satisfy this, and German B2 plus an audiogram are hard gates.

programs.university: École supérieure d'art et de design TALM — site du Mans (ESAD TALM-Le Mans), with IRCAM, ENSCI-Les Ateliers and Le Mans Université / LAUM
programs.degree: DNSEP (Diplôme National Supérieur d'Expression Plastique) conférant le grade de master
programs.durationEcts: 2 years (années 4 and 5, semesters 7-10). ECTS total UNVERIFIED (French DNSEP = 120 ECTS at 2nd cycle).
programs.focus: Sound Design (industrial, object, environmental, multimodal) + Sonic Arts + some Immersive/Spatial Audio
programs.institutionType: Public art and design school (école supérieure d'art), in partnership with a research institute (IRCAM), a design school (ENSCI) and a university acoustics lab (LAUM/CNRS)
programs.language: French (a compulsory 'Anglais, le langage comme matière, matériau et matériel' module in UE3)
programs.whatYouStudy: Semesters 7 and 9 modules: 'Création sonore appliquée', 'Workshop applicatif', 'Production, diffusion et perception du son, appliquées au design sonore', 'Informatique sonore et technique son', 'Workshop arduino', 'Méthodologie créative en design sonore', 'Atelier Radio', 'Éléments scientifiques', 'Concepts de design et cognition auditive appliqués au design sonore', 'Histoire et théorie du sonore', 'Ateliers de recherche et création (ARC)', 'Anthropocène : usage et mésusage du monde', histoire des arts, pratique professionnelle, pré-mémoire then mémoire. Semester 8 is international exchange or a company placement. Semester 10 = mémoire and plastic-work defence before a jury of professionals. The year opens with a two-week 'workshop applicatif' answering a real brief from an industrial or institutional partner, in mixed teams with ENSCI design students — past clients: Décathlon, SETRAM/Le Mans Métropole tram sonification, Groupe PSA (gestural and sound interfaces), SNCF Direction Innovation, Maison de la Radio / Radio France, RATP, GHT Psychiatrie Sainte-Anne. Students also run '24 heures' of radio on the school station Radio-on and produce work for Le Mans Sonore, the city's international sound biennial.
programs.entryRequirements: 'Ce DNSEP s'adresse à tout type de créat.eurs.rices sonores, designers, musicien.ne.s, composit.eurs.rices, artistes, dont la pratique sonore et musicale peut s'adapter aux champs d'application très divers du design sonore.' Accepted profiles: 'Le.la candidat.e peut être diplômé.e d'une filière artistique ou d'électroacoustique des universités (ou être inscrit.e en licence au moment du concours - titre RNCP niveau II -) ; d'une école d'art ou de design équivalent au niveau licence (DNA ou équivalents étrangers) ; d'une école d'enseignement musical spécialisé équivalent au niveau licence (DNSPM ou équivalents étrangers), d'un DEM de composition ou électroacoustique d'un établissement musical spécialisé agréé par l'État, à condition de posséder en plus une licence scientifique ou en sciences humaines.' Selection criteria: 'La motivation, l'ouverture d'esprit, la faculté d'adaptation à des contextes spécifiques, le potentiel à travailler en équipe'. About ten places ('accessible à une dizaine de jeunes diplômé.e.s').
programs.portfolioSpec: Two-stage commission. 'La phase de pré-sélection se déroule sans la présence du.de la candidat.e et comporte une seule épreuve : l'évaluation du dossier personnel de candidature par la commission d'admissibilité — composée du directeur de TALM-Le Mans et d'au moins trois intervenant.e.s de la mention Design sonore — avec un examen approfondi des éléments fournis'. The jury reads 'votre portfolio envoyé pour la présélection'. The exact number of works, durations and file formats are NOT specified in the official presentation document — UNVERIFIED; request the current concours notice from contact-lemans@talm.fr.
programs.auditionSpec: 'La phase d'admission' — admissible candidates present a personal dossier before a jury which has already read the portfolio; 'les membres de la commission évaluent la motivation du.de la candidat.e, son goût pour la création, sa curiosité intellectuelle, sa capacité à être en prise avec les enjeux contemporains, ainsi que sa capacité à développer une réflexion et une pratique personnelle.' On-site interview at Le Mans. Dates for the 2027 entry UNVERIFIED.
programs.acceptsNonMusic: CHECK — probably not on its own. The published list of accepted diplomas is art, design, university electroacoustic/artistic filières, DNSPM or a DEM in composition/electroacoustics. A scientific licence appears only as an ADDITIONAL condition attached to the DEM route ('à condition de posséder en plus une licence scientifique ou en sciences humaines'), not as a standalone qualification. A software-engineering BSc with no artistic or electroacoustic credential is therefore not clearly eligible; the school does, however, open the programme to 'tout type de créateurs sonores ... dont la pratique sonore et musicale peut s'adapter'. Ask the school in writing before applying.
programs.applicationOpens: UNVERIFIED — no 2027 concours calendar found on the pages read.
programs.deadline: UNVERIFIED — no published date for the 2027 entry. (The public art-school concours cycle in France typically runs January-May.) Contact contact-lemans@talm.fr / 02 72 16 48 78.
programs.tuitionIntl: UNVERIFIED — no figure on the documents read. Public écoles supérieures d'art typically charge several hundred euros per year plus CVEC, but the differentiated non-EU regime for écoles d'art was not confirmed.
programs.scholarship: None found in the official presentation document.
programs.facilities: 'Studio son, équipé d'une écoute en 5.1'; multitrack digital recorders, an ambisonic microphone, an octophonic diffusion system, assorted microphones, audio interfaces, amplifiers and loudspeakers; MIDI controllers and a radio studio; plus full art-school workshops (volume, photography, video, engraving and print, painting, casting, mechatronics). Partners: IRCAM (Labo STMS and Perception & Design Sonores team — Nicolas Misdariis, Patrick Susini), ENSCI-Les Ateliers Paris (Roland Cahen, sound studio), Le Mans Université's LAUM (CNRS). Teaching team: Olivier Houix (IRCAM researcher, coordinator), Rodolphe Alexis, Fabien Bourdier, Ludovic Germain (ENSCI graduate, founder of the LAPS sound-design agency). Host of Le Mans Sonore biennial.
programs.fitNotes: Exceptional industry exposure — real briefs from SNCF, RATP, PSA, Radio France — and the IRCAM/ENSCI/LAUM triangle is unique in Europe. But the discipline is FUNCTIONAL sound design (product, transport, museum, UX signage), not music production, and the admissions list is built around art/design/electroacoustic diplomas. For a CS graduate aiming at DJ/producer work this is both a fit mismatch and an eligibility risk; it would suit him far better if he first built an art/sound portfolio and if the school confirms in writing that a scientific licence plus a strong sound portfolio is admissible.

programs.program: Master Acoustique et musicologie — parcours Ingénierie et conception sonore
programs.university: Aix-Marseille Université (AMU), Faculté des Sciences / UFR ALLSH
programs.city: Marseille (campus Saint-Charles), with some sessions in Aix-en-Provence
programs.durationEcts: 2 years / 4 semesters / 120 ECTS (30 per semester)
programs.focus: Sound Design + Immersive/Spatial Audio + Recording/Engineering, with a strong acoustics and signal-processing spine
programs.institutionType: Public university
programs.language: French (C1 minimum for non-French speakers); English B2 minimum required
programs.whatYouStudy: Semester 1 is a common core with the musicology side, then specialisation into Ingénierie et conception sonore from semester 2. Modules: physical acoustics and signal processing; perception and cognition; computer programming and software development; sound and music listening practices; collective projects and field schools; compulsory 5-month internship in semester 4.
programs.entryRequirements: Selection on dossier via monmaster.gouv.fr. 'Licences conseillées: Physique, sciences et technologies, mathématiques, informatique, mécanique, MPCI (Mathématiques, physique, chimie, informatique), sciences pour l'ingénieur.' Language: French C1 minimum for non-French speakers, English B2 minimum. Capacity UNVERIFIED.
programs.portfolioSpec: No portfolio requirement published on the programme page — selection is on academic dossier (transcripts, motivation) through monmaster.gouv.fr. UNVERIFIED whether a personal project or sound works may be attached; check the mention's 'critères d'examen des candidatures' on monmaster when the 2027 campaign opens.
programs.auditionSpec: None published — no live audition, no on-site test mentioned. Selection appears to be dossier-only. UNVERIFIED whether an interview is used.
programs.acceptsNonMusic: YES, explicitly and unusually favourably. The recommended bachelor list names 'informatique' and 'sciences pour l'ingénieur' directly, and the syllabus assumes programming ability. This is one of the few French sound masters where a software-engineering BSc is the INTENDED entry profile rather than an exception.
programs.applicationOpens: PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new date: national monmaster.gouv.fr campaign for M1 typically opens late February. The programme page's indicative timeline shows applications March-April, review April-June, admission June-July (2023 cycle shown).
programs.deadline: PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new date — the page shows only an old indicative March-April window. The 2027 deadline will be set by the national monmaster.gouv.fr calendar (published each winter).

programs.fundingLevel: Partial to full depending on the differentiated-fee exemption (which is a university-level decision, capped nationally at 30% of affected students in 2026-2027 and 25% in 2027-2028).
programs.scholarship: None programme-specific found. Realistic vehicles: France Excellence Eiffel (€1,181/month at master level, age limit 25 for master, nominated BY the institution — the 2026 call closed 8 January 2026, so the 2027 call will likely close early January 2027); Campus France Tunisie / French Embassy bourses; AMU international scholarships UNVERIFIED.

programs.facilities: AMU acoustics and musicology environment, Saint-Charles campus in central Marseille; field schools and collective projects; 5-month industry internship. Studio/console inventory UNVERIFIED.
programs.fitNotes: The best 'front door' in France for exactly his degree: the programme asks for a physics/maths/informatique licence, is dossier-only (no live audition, no music theory test), costs public-university money, and is in a major city. The caveat is orientation — the mention is 'Acoustique et musicologie', so expect a heavier scientific and perceptual load (signal processing, cognition, acoustics) than hands-on beat-making; production craft will come from the projects and the internship rather than from a mixing studio curriculum. Strong first-choice candidate, but he should pair it with a portfolio of his own tracks to argue the creative side, and check the differentiated-fee exemption early.

programs.program: Master Cinéma et Audiovisuel — parcours Ingénierie du son à l'image (département SATIS)
programs.university: Aix-Marseille Université — Faculté des Sciences, département SATIS
programs.durationEcts: 2 years (M1 + M2); entry requires 180 ECTS for M1, 240 ECTS for M2. Programme ECTS UNVERIFIED (French master = 120 ECTS).
programs.focus: Film/Game Sound + Recording/Engineering (son à l'image, multichannel mixing, live capture)
programs.institutionType: Public university film school (described as France's fourth public higher film school)
programs.language: French — C1 level required for international students
programs.whatYouStudy: Production-driven curriculum on professional equipment in professional configurations. M1: 5 fiction shorts shot on Super 16mm, 5 documentaries, multicamera capture work. M2: 2 fiction shorts (15 min, HD, multichannel mix), 1 cine-concert, 1 documentary (26 min, HD). Plus a placement of 6 months or more. SATIS teaches five specialities side by side — image, sound, music, editing, production/directing — so sound students work inside real crews.
programs.entryRequirements: M1 entry: 'Licence, 180 ECTS et 4 semaines de stage dans le secteur'. Candidates 'doivent avoir un projet professionnel (appuyé par une première expérience professionnelle d'au moins un mois dans le domaine de l'audiovisuel : convention de stage et rapport d'activité) et une forte motivation'. M2 entry: M1 Cinéma/Audiovisuel, 240 ECTS, 8 weeks of prior sector experience. French C1 for international students.
programs.portfolioSpec: No creative portfolio of finished works is specified. Instead the decisive documents are the professional project statement plus PROOF of at least one month of audiovisual-sector experience (internship agreement + activity report) and 4 weeks of sector internship. UNVERIFIED whether personal sound works may be attached.
programs.auditionSpec: 'Le recrutement se fait sur dossier, QCM et entretien' — application file, a multiple-choice test and an interview. No instrumental audition. Test content and location UNVERIFIED (likely on site in Aubagne).
programs.acceptsNonMusic: YES on the diploma (any 'Licence, 180 ECTS' is the stated requirement — no music or audiovisual degree named), BUT there is a hard non-academic condition a fresh CS graduate will fail today: four weeks of sector internship plus at least one month of documented professional experience in audiovisual, with an internship agreement and activity report. He would need to arrange an audio/audiovisual internship in 2026 to be eligible at all.

programs.tuitionIntl: Public university fees; non-EU 'droits différenciés' of ~€3,950/yr for master in 2026-2027 may apply unless exempted (AMU policy UNVERIFIED). Plus CVEC.

Two frictions: the mandatory documented audiovisual work experience before applying (a 2026 to-do, not a 2027 one), and the film-and-television orientation, which trains a boom operator/re-recording mixer rather than a music producer. Good backup if he can land an audio internship in Tunisia or France during 2026; weak fit for the DJ goal.

programs.program: Master Cinéma et audiovisuel — parcours Son (ENSAV)
programs.university: Université Toulouse - Jean Jaurès / École Nationale Supérieure d'AudioVisuel (ENSAV, formerly ESAV)
programs.durationEcts: 2 years (M1 + M2). ECTS for the programme UNVERIFIED; M1 entry requires 180 ECTS, M2 entry 240 ECTS.
programs.focus: Film Sound + Sound Design + Recording (practice-based, very production-heavy)
programs.institutionType: Public university film school (école interne of Université Toulouse - Jean Jaurès)
programs.language: French
programs.whatYouStudy: Roughly 15 compulsory exercises over the two years — sound pieces, documentaries and fiction works, each with defined pedagogical constraints — plus a personal film at the end of M1 and of M2 with no restriction on genre or duration, each accompanied by a methodological dissertation. Taught content covers acoustic principles, analogue and digital audio technology, sound recording, mixing and distribution/diffusion techniques.
programs.entryRequirements: 'Licence Création Audiovisuelle ou d'une formation bac+3 équivalente dans les domaines des arts, des arts du spectacle, de l'architecture, du design, des arts plastiques, DE L'INFORMATIQUE ou des beaux-arts.' M1 candidates need Bac+3 / 180 ECTS; M2 entrants 240 ECTS. Admission is at the end of L3 plus selection on dossier; 'à l'issue de l'examen du dossier, un entretien peut être programmé avec le candidat'. Dossiers are emailed to ensav@univ-tlse2.fr (the Production parcours uses monmaster; the son route is handled by ENSAV directly).

Request the son-specific dossier from ensav@univ-tlse2.fr.
programs.auditionSpec: Selection on dossier, with a possible interview after the file review ('un entretien peut être programmé'). No live audition or written concours found. UNVERIFIED whether the interview is remote or on site.
programs.acceptsNonMusic: YES, and this is the clearest positive wording found anywhere in this slice: the accepted bachelor list explicitly includes 'DE L'INFORMATIQUE'. A Bac+3 in computer science is a named, accepted entry qualification. No music degree, no audition, no music-theory test.
programs.applicationOpens: PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new date: the ENSAV M1 dossier for 2026-2027 was posted in March 2026.
programs.deadline: PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new date. 2026-2027 cycle: dossiers due 10 May 2026 (M2 REX: 31 August 2026); the M1 Production route on Mon Master closed 16 March 2026. Confirm the 2027-2028 son deadline with ensav@univ-tlse2.fr.
programs.tuitionIntl: Public university fees; non-EU 'droits différenciés' of ~€3,950/yr for master in 2026-2027 may apply unless exempted (Toulouse Jean Jaurès policy UNVERIFIED). Plus CVEC. Not stated on the programme page — UNVERIFIED.
programs.fundingLevel: Partial to full depending on differentiated-fee exemption; no stipend.
programs.scholarship: None programme-specific found. External: France Excellence Eiffel (institution-nominated, master age cap 25, €1,181/month + air ticket + social cover; the 2026 call closed 8 Jan 2026), Campus France Tunisie.

Realistic primary or secondary target, and probably his highest-probability admission among the public film schools.

programs.program: Master Ingénierie de l'image, ingénierie du son — parcours Image et Son (ISB)
programs.university: Université de Bretagne Occidentale (UBO), Faculté des Sciences et Techniques — Image & Son Brest
programs.degree: Master (mention Ingénierie de l'image, ingénierie du son)
programs.durationEcts: 2 years, semesters 7-10, approximately 60 ECTS per year (total 120). Stated as 'approximately 60 credits per year'.
programs.focus: Recording/Engineering + Immersive/Spatial Audio + Music Production (studio) + film/AV post-production
programs.institutionType: Public university (science faculty), engineering-oriented sound and image school
programs.language: French
programs.whatYouStudy: Sound modules: 'Electroacoustique & Acoustique des salles'; 'Traitement du signal audionumérique'; studio practice in recording, mixing and mastering; 'Son spatialisé' (stereo, object-based and binaural formats); music informatics; classical sound recording. Image and post-production courses run alongside across both years. Graduates go into audiovisual and cinema (lighting, editing, sound, post-production) and into music careers — recording studios and live events.
programs.entryRequirements: M1: an L3 in the SPI mention with the 'Image & Son' specialisation 'ou équivalent', assessed after examination of the dossier and an interview. The programme notes that students normally follow the full L3 to M1 to M2 path rather than joining at M1. M2: continuation of the M1 Image et Son 'or equivalent master', again on dossier plus interview. Capacity: 'La limitation à 18 étudiants par promotion'. Total school enrolment about 50 students; the school reports 100% professional insertion 18 months after the M2.
programs.portfolioSpec: No portfolio of works specified — selection is 'examen du dossier de candidature et entretien'. Whether personal sound work can be attached is UNVERIFIED; the school's own admissions page does not list the dossier contents.
programs.auditionSpec: No audition. An interview ('entretien') follows the dossier review for both M1 and M2. Format and location UNVERIFIED.
programs.acceptsNonMusic: CHECK — leaning yes but not proven. The requirement is an L3 in Sciences pour l'Ingénieur with the Image & Son specialisation 'or equivalent'. A software-engineering BSc is scientifically adjacent, and the master's own spine is signal processing and electroacoustics, but the page also warns that entry at M1 is unusual because most students come up through the in-house L3. The school does not publish any wording accepting non-specialised science degrees. He must email the ISB to test eligibility before applying.
programs.applicationOpens: PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new date: M1 applications for 2026-2027 opened 17 February 2026 on monmaster; L3 and M2 applications opened 27 April 2026 on eCandidat.
programs.deadline: PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new date. 2026-2027: M1 window 17 February - 16 March 2026 (monmaster.gouv.fr); L3 and M2 window 27 April - 31 May 2026 (eCandidat UBO). The 2027 M1 window will follow the national monmaster calendar.
programs.tuitionIntl: Public university fees. UBO publishes a 'Droits d'inscription différenciés' notice — content not read, so the non-EU rate and exemption policy are UNVERIFIED. National differentiated master rate for 2026-2027 is about €3,950/yr where applied. Plus CVEC.
programs.fundingLevel: Partial to full depending on the differentiated-fee exemption; no stipend.
programs.scholarship: None programme-specific found. External: France Excellence Eiffel (institution-nominated), Campus France Tunisie / Embassy bourses.
programs.facilities: Studio practice for recording, mixing and mastering; spatial audio work across stereo, object-based and binaural formats; music-informatics teaching; cohort capped at 18 so studio access is high per student. Reported 100% employment 18 months post-M2. Console/room inventory UNVERIFIED.
programs.fitNotes: Technically the closest French public master to a 'sound engineer' training with real music-studio content (recording, mixing, mastering, spatialisation) and a very small cohort. Two frictions: the programme is designed as a continuation of its own L3, so a direct M1 entry from a Tunisian CS degree needs a case-by-case ruling, and Brest is remote from any electronic-music scene. Worth an early eligibility email; if they accept him, the curriculum-to-goal alignment is among the best in the slice.

programs.program: Erasmus Mundus Joint Master DIGICREA — Digital Creativity, Art & Science, SOUND-MUSIC specialization
programs.university: Consortium: Université Jean Monnet Saint-Étienne (coordinator, France) + Universidade Católica Portuguesa Porto (Portugal) + University of Silesia Katowice/Cieszyn (Poland)
programs.degree: Erasmus Mundus Joint Master — multiple degrees awarded by Université Jean Monnet, Universidade Católica Portuguesa and University of Silesia
programs.durationEcts: 2 years / 4 semesters across three countries, ending with an internship. ECTS total UNVERIFIED (EMJM standard = 120).
programs.focus: Electronic Music / Music Production + Sound Design + digital creation (there is a dedicated SOUND-MUSIC specialization path, distinct from the IMAGE path)
programs.language: English — 'The entire program is taught in English.'
programs.institutionType: Public university consortium (Erasmus Mundus Joint Master, EU-funded)
programs.whatYouStudy: Training in audiovisual new media, emerging technologies in the film industry, music, graphic design, artificial intelligence, virtual reality and their applications. Two specialization paths: SOUND-MUSIC and IMAGE; all candidates apply to one only. The Selection Board 'assesses the candidate's predispositions for professions related to the production of audio-visual and musical forms, including the production of Extended Reality films'. Mobility: Saint-Étienne, then Porto, then Katowice, then an internship with public and private sector partners. The programme shares courses with the Université Jean Monnet Master CCNT (Création Contemporaine et Nouvelles Technologies, RIM/Arts numériques), so the Saint-Étienne semester connects to the RIM music-computing environment. Detailed module list UNVERIFIED.
programs.entryRequirements: 'A Bachelor's degree of at least 180 ECTS is the minimum requirement to enrol' — no field restriction stated. Candidates with at least 150 ECTS at application may be considered with a sworn statement that 180 ECTS will be obtained before the start. Documents: EUROPASS CV in English; proof of nationality; certified copies (with certified English translations) of higher-education and high-school diplomas and full transcripts; at least two letters of recommendation in English on letterhead, signed and stamped, with referee contacts; a 'Science qualification and experience in New Technology' form in which candidates 'describe their level in mathematics, digital signal processing, and computer science ... their skills and level in JavaScript, Python or C, HTML, real-time graphics programming, geometry, trigonometric functions, and algebra courses'; English certificate at minimum B2, C1 recommended (IELTS 6, TOEFL iBT ≥90, TOEFL ITP 550, TOEIC ≥650, or a degree taught 100% in English with a university letter). Applications via the UJM eCandidat portal — explicitly NOT via Études en France.
programs.portfolioSpec: 'Artistic or Professional Portfolio: Document presenting artistic productions related to the DIGICREA curriculum and specialization path chosen by the applicant. All projects included in the portfolio must not be more than 5 years old. Submit EXACTLY 3 TO 5 specific works or project (video/audio/images) including metadata (title, short description, public link, and their role): minimum 3 works - maximum 5 works. Please number works presented in the portfolio from 1 to 5.' For Sound-Music applicants 'it can be a composition project (orchestral or electronic), sound design project, sound concept project, music piece cycle, demo, etc.' The PDF is capped at 5 MB, so online links are used for the media. Also required in place of a cover letter: a VIDEO PRESENTATION of maximum 2 minutes covering, in order, current situation, motivation for applying, understanding of the programme, why the candidate can succeed, and ideas for applied research and professional development — link supplied in a PDF 'Motivation letter' item, accessible to anyone with the link until mid-April.
programs.auditionSpec: Stage II: shortlisted applicants only, an ONLINE 15-minute interview (2026 cycle: forecast 24-30 March 2026) assessing 'the candidate's personality characteristics, way of thinking, personal life experience, and character attributes'. Candidates may additionally be asked to attend a videoconference to verify English level. No on-site test, no live audition, no travel needed to apply.
programs.acceptsNonMusic: YES — the strongest case in this slice. The only academic requirement is 'A Bachelor's degree of at least 180 ECTS', with no field restriction, and the application actively rewards a software background: a compulsory form asks the candidate to rate their level in mathematics, digital signal processing and computer science, and specifically in JavaScript, Python or C, HTML, real-time graphics programming, geometry, trigonometry and algebra. A software-engineering graduate with a music portfolio is close to the ideal applicant profile.
programs.applicationOpens: 2027 CYCLE: 'The call for applications for the next DIGICREA cohort 2027-2029 is expected to open in November 2026. Further information regarding this procedure will be available in the autumn. Please note that some requirements will differ from those of the 2026 selection process.'
programs.deadline: 2027 intake not yet fixed. PRIOR CYCLE reference: the 2026-2028 call opened 14 November 2025 and closed 16 February 2026, with Stage II interviews forecast 24-30 March 2026 — expect a comparable mid-February 2027 deadline. Confirm from November 2026.
programs.tuitionIntl: ZERO. 'Students (scholarship holders and non-scholarship holders) are not charged any tuition fees.' Self-funded students must submit a Guarantee of full financial support with a budget simulation, and document their income for the visa.
programs.fundingLevel: Full (for scholarship holders) — the best funding on offer in this slice
programs.scholarship: Erasmus Mundus Joint Master (EMJM) scholarship: 'a grant of 1,400 euros per month, for a total duration of 24 months. The maximum amount per student is therefore 1,400 euros x 24 months = 33,600 euros', awarded for full-time enrolment over the whole course, covering travel, visa, installation and subsistence, paid into the student's own bank account.
